spHawkes: Semi-Parametric Self-Exciting Point Process Models

Source: R/spHawkes-package.R
spHawkes-package.Rd

Fits semi-parametric spatio-temporal Hawkes (self-exciting) point process models to event data via a stochastic-declustering EM algorithm (Zhuang & Mateu, 2019), on any sf point layer and study-region polygon.

The conditional intensity is the sum of a background term, capturing baseline place-based risk, and a triggering term, capturing the extra risk each past event induces nearby in space and soon after in time: $$\lambda(x, y, t \mid H_t) = \mu_0 \, \mu_T(t) \, \mu_m(t) \, \mu_w(t) \, \mu_b(x, y) + A \int_{-\infty}^{t} \int_{W} g(t - s) \, h(x - u, y - v) \, N(du \, dv \, ds),$$ where \(W\) is the study region and \(N\) is the counting measure of the events, so the triggering term adds up \(A \, g(t - t_i) \, h(x - x_i, y - y_i)\) over the events \(i\) before \(t\). The background factors (long-term trend, calendar month, day of week, and a spatial surface) and both triggering kernels are estimated non-parametrically; \(\mu_0\) and the branching ratio \(A\) are updated in closed form.

Getting started

vignette("getting-started", package = "spHawkes") walks through the whole workflow on a small example dataset.

The usual entry point is fit_semihawkes(), which runs the full pipeline from raw sf points to a converged fit. The stages it composes are also exported individually, so a single step can be inspected without running the whole EM loop:

Data preparation

prepare_events(), add_adaptive_bandwidth(), add_bg_integral()

Background components

temporal_base_trend(), temporal_base_weekly(), temporal_base_monthly(), background_spatial(), background_intensity()

Triggering components

trigger_temporal_init(), trigger_spatial_init(), trigger_evaluate(), trigger_reestimate_temporal(), trigger_reestimate_spatial()

EM

em_step() for one iteration, fit_semihawkes() to convergence

Branching structure & uncertainty

sample_branching(), sample_branching_multi(), check_branching_weights(), summarize_branching_samples() – stochastic declustering / Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification for which events are background vs. triggered; see vignette("branching-structure-uq", package = "spHawkes")

Diagnostics

background_trigger_grid() for gridded background/triggering intensity snapshots over time, the building block for exceedance-set and persistence analyses

sim_events and sim_region are a small simulated dataset for trying the above out.

In the code

spHawkes began as a port of the R code that accompanies D'Angelo et al. (2024), which implements the method of Zhuang and Mateu (2019). It has since been substantially rewritten: several errors in that code have been fixed, and its slowest computations have been rewritten to run much faster. The model and the estimation method are the same.

Units and scale

Every distance and bandwidth in the package is in the linear units of the working CRS, and the defaults were tuned for a metre-based projection of a city-scale dataset. prepare_events() rejects geographic (longitude and latitude) input for this reason, and warns when the CRS units are not metres. Applying the package to a different study area means re-choosing cell_size, the triggering-kernel grid extents, and the smoothing bandwidths to suit it; see the vignette's final section.

References

Zhuang, J. and Mateu, J. (2019). A semiparametric spatiotemporal Hawkes-type point process model with periodic background for crime data. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A, 182(3), 919-942. doi:10.1111/rssa.12429

Zhuang, J., Ogata, Y. and Vere-Jones, D. (2002). Stochastic declustering of space-time earthquake occurrences. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 97(458), 369-380. doi:10.1198/016214502760046925

D'Angelo, N., Payares, D., Adelfio, G., and Mateu, J. (2024). Self-exciting point process modelling of crimes on linear networks. Statistical Modelling, 24(2), 139–168. doi:10.1177/1471082X221094146 .
